Multi-zone PDM

Source: R/multizone.R
two_zone_config.Rd

A multi-zone PDM divides the catchment into hydrological zones, each a complete PDM with its own parameters, area and delay, driven by the same rainfall and evaporation; their flows are added at the outlet (PDM for PCs configuration guide, section 5). It gives a catchment a third timescale where one PDM's two routes are not enough: a sharp spike over a few hours, then a slower flood hydrograph, then baseflow.

Usage

two_zone_config(config, share = 0.1, names = c("main", "fast"))

FlodeMultiZoneModel(zones = list(), area_km2 = integer(0), dt = integer(0))

FlodeMultiZoneState(states = list())

Arguments

config

A single-zone configuration.

share

Starting share of the catchment area for the fast zone.

names

Names of the two zones.

Value

two_zone_config(): a multi-zone configuration for pdm_from_config().

Details

Configuration. A multi-zone configuration has area_km2 and dt for the whole catchment, optionally one rainfall factor fc for every zone, and a named list zones, each a single-zone configuration without area_km2 or dt (nor fc, when it is given at the top). Every zone after the first has a share, its fraction of the catchment area; the first zone takes the rest. Parameters are addressed as zones.<name>.<path>, such as zones.fast.share or zones.main.surface.k1.

The fast zone. two_zone_config() adds a zone for the spike to a single-zone configuration, with every parameter set and most of them locked:

ParameterValueSearched
share0.1 of the area0.01 to 0.3
soil storePareto, cmax 20 mm, b 0.5cmax, 1 to 100 mm
rechargesplit, alpha 1: all direct runoff to the surface, none to groundwaterno
surfaceone linear store, kb 1 hkb, 0.25 to 12 h
groundwaterlinear, kb 1000 h, never fedno
td0 h0 to 6 h
bethe main zone'sno

The rain adds up. Every zone reads the same rain and evaporation depths, and the zone areas add up to the catchment's, so the rain volume over the zones is the catchment's. The rainfall factor fc is set once, at the top, for every zone (locked at 1 by default, as for one zone); unlocked with overrides = list(fc = ...), it scales the rain on every zone together.

The fast zone only ever makes quick runoff, so it cannot trade baseflow with the main zone, which keeps the two zones' roles apart. calibration_bounds() gives the main zone its usual bounds and the fast zone the four above; bounds or exclusions given without a zones. prefix apply to the first zone.

Running. run_pdm() runs each zone with its own state and adds the flows; depth columns (rain, storage, balance) are area-weighted means over the zones. A start from flow puts the whole observed flow on the first zone and starts the others with their soil at soil_fraction and their routing stores empty. Forecast updating, hindcasts, the events workbench and PDM for PCs files are for single-zone models.

References

Moore, R.J. (2007). The PDM rainfall-runoff model. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 11(1), 483-499. UKCEH (2022). PDM for PCs, version 3.0.3: Configuration Guide, section 5.

Examples

cfg <- pdm_presets("standard")
cfg$area_km2 <- 36.7
two <- two_zone_config(cfg)
model <- pdm_from_config(two)
calibration_bounds(two)[, c("path", "lower", "upper")]
#>                            path  lower   upper
#> 1  zones.main.distribution.cmax  20.00 8.0e+02
#> 2     zones.main.distribution.b   0.05 2.0e+00
#> 3        zones.main.recharge.kg   1.00 5.0e+03
#> 4         zones.main.surface.k1   0.50 7.2e+01
#> 5         zones.main.surface.k2   0.50 7.2e+01
#> 6     zones.main.groundwater.kb 100.00 1.0e+06
#> 7              zones.fast.share   0.01 3.0e-01
#> 8  zones.fast.distribution.cmax   1.00 1.0e+02
#> 9         zones.fast.surface.kb   0.25 1.2e+01
#> 10                zones.fast.td   0.00 6.0e+00
